#### Non-Oauth apps
```bash
appcfg apps config create <application identifier> \
--name "My Configuration" \
--config '{"non-secret":"configuration", "host":"www.example.com"}' \
--secrets '{"a-secret":"api-token"}' \
--activate
```
> [!NOTE]
> Tip
>
> The `—config` flag is required even if the configuration is empty

results.title: Generate API Tokens and Create Webhooks
results.snippet:
API tokens are required to use Gladly APIs for security and authentication purposes. Tokens can be accessed and created by users who at least have an API user [role](https://help.gladly.com/docs/managing-users-and-roles).
## Before you start
- For integrations not built by Gladly, a Gladly Administrator should [create](https://help.gladly.com/docs/managing-users-and-roles) a new user with an API role + Agent and/or Administrator (check with your integration partner to confirm the required roles) account for *each* integration. This account should be used to access Gladly to create the API tokens or webhooks.
- The integration partner should provide the email address to be used with the integration's user account in Gladly. They must also access emails from this account to activate their Gladly account to create API tokens or webhooks.
- API tokens are tied to a single user account and a particular environment. For example, an API token attached to Gladly user *developer@customer.com* in the Sandbox environment is not valid for *developer@customer.com* in the Production environment.

results.snippet:
## REST API
Clients can access the **REST API** via HTTPS at your organization's Gladly domain (e.g. `https://{organization}.gladly.com`).
Resources follow REST semantics and utilize industry-standard HTTP verbs, response codes, and authentication schemes. In addition, all responses and payloads are in JSON with consistent error codes and formats.
## Lookup API
The Gladly **Lookup API** allows your organization to provide data services to power the agent's experience with a complete view of your customers' information, transactions, and activity. You can provide a web service that implements the Lookup API and Gladly will call it when that data is needed.
Like the REST API, the Lookup API is specified using REST semantics, and exchanges JSON requests and responses authenticated and signed with secure keys.
Gladly will perform lookups when certain activities occur within Gladly, such as when a customer's profile is loaded.

Your sandbox environment is accessible at `https://{organization}.gladly.qa`, where `organization` is your company name. For specific API endpoints, see documentation below.

results.title: help.gladly.com/developer-tutorials/docs/data-pulls-1
results.snippet:
Data Pulls in the Gladly App Platform allow you to extend your customer view by retrieving and integrating data from external systems into Gladly.

The App Platform uses a combination of configuration files, Go templates, and GraphQL schemas to define how data is retrieved, transformed, and made available within Gladly.
## Using Data Pulls
Currently, Data Pulls are available in:
- Customer Profile (displayed using Cards)
- Sidekick
- Routing
- Rules
### Use Cases
Data Pulls should be used any time you want to retrieve data that is connected with a Customer. For example:
- Order Management: getting Customer’s order history
- Routing based on Customer Lifetime value

An App can be configured to pull data from external systems. Data Pulls are used throughout Gladly and this data can be used to assist Agents and allow Customers to self-serve via Sidekick.

- Identify the inputs and outputs of the REST APIs for the data you wish to bring into Gladly.
- Use the appcfg tool tool to create the request URL, headers, and/or body go templates.

Gladys can connect to your favourite AI assistant through the **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**. Once connected, your assistant accesses the data you already see in Gladys and can act for you: check your tasks, write a meeting report, answer a question about a project, etc.

## Getting the connector address
The **Connect an AI** area shows the unique address of your Gladys connector, to copy and paste into your assistant's settings:
```
https://mcp.gladys.com/
```
This address is the same whichever assistant you choose.
**The AI only accesses the data you already see in Gladys** — it can neither see nor change more than what you yourself have access to.

Gladys Assistant integrates an MCP server that enables your compatible AI agents (Claude Desktop, Perplexity, Mistral Le Chat, etc.) to communicate with your smart home. Currently available capabilities include:

- volume
- 📷 View your cameras and describe what it sees (if your client is compatible)
- 💡 Turn lights on/off
- 🔌 Control switches and outlets
- 🎬 Launch scenes
The MCP system works with 2 components:
1. **The MCP client**: This is your AI agent (Claude Desktop, Perplexity, Mistral Le Chat...)
2. **The MCP server**: Integrated into Gladys, it exposes available functions that the client can call
